# A2 escalation rule: category-based cascade (draft)

**Status:** draft. Commit before the first A2 benchmark run, together with the prediction record; not revised after.
**Evidence:** `analysis/output/a2_tuning.md`, generated by `python analysis/a2_tuning.py` from the **tuning set only**
(`datasets/a2/tuning_set.csv`, 87 tickets, odd rows). The test set was not used to choose anything below.

## Models

| Role | Ollama tag | Digest | Call |
|---|---|---|---|
| Small (first) | `phi3:3.8b` | `4f222292793889a9a40a020799cfd28d53f3e01af25d48e06c5e708610fc47e9` | prompt v1, temperature 0, seed 42, JSON format restricted to the 7 categories |
| Large (escalation) | `gemma4:e4b` | `c6eb396dbd5992bbe3f5cdb947e8bbc0ee413d7c17e2beaae69f5d569cf982eb` | identical call; `think` not sent, so gemma4 thinks as in A1 |

Both models stay resident in the one Docker Ollama (`OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=2`, `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1`,
`OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1`, held constant for every A2 configuration). Memory check on the SUT: PASS, both resident
through 6 alternating tickets with no reload, about 3.5 GiB left (`tests/environment/a2_memcheck/`).

## The rule

For each ticket, inside `POST /tickets`:

1. Send the narrative to **phi3:3.8b** with the unchanged v1 classification prompt. Call its answer `C`.
2. If `C` is one of the setting's **accept list**, return `C`. The ticket is **not escalated**; final model = phi3.
3. Otherwise (phi3 answered a category outside the accept list, or gave no valid category), send the same narrative
   with the same prompt to **gemma4:e4b** and return its answer, even if it differs from `C`. The ticket is
   **escalated**; final model = gemma4. If gemma4 also fails, the request fails exactly as in A1 (HTTP 502).

The rule uses only phi3's predicted category, because the true category is unknown when a ticket arrives. It adds
no extra model call: an accepted ticket costs one phi3 call, an escalated ticket one phi3 call plus one gemma4 call.
The response body is the same as in A1, so the caller cannot tell which model answered.

## Settings tested

| Setting | Accept phi3's answer when it predicts | Escalate when it predicts | How the list was chosen |
|---|---|---|---|
| **S1 (cautious)** | Consumer loan, Debt collection, Credit card, Money transfer or service | Mortgage, Credit reporting, Bank account or service | categories where every phi3 answer on the tuning set was right (precision 100%) |
| **S2 (faster)** | S1 + Mortgage | Credit reporting, Bank account or service | categories with tuning precision of at least 85% |

## Why this rule

On the tuning set phi3 is right on 70 of 87 tickets (80.5%), and its 17 errors sit in three **predicted**
categories, so the predicted category is a usable signal:

| phi3 predicted | Tickets | Correct | Wrong ones are really |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bank account or service | 21 | 12 (57%) | Money transfer 5, Credit card 2, Debt collection 1, Consumer loan 1 |
| Credit reporting | 19 | 14 (74%) | Debt collection 4, Credit card 1 |
| Mortgage | 20 | 17 (85%) | Consumer loan 2, Credit reporting 1 |
| Consumer loan / Debt collection / Credit card / Money transfer | 12 / 8 / 5 / 2 | all correct | - |

Estimated on the tuning set (gemma4 answers from A1, thinking on; latency = 2.1 s phi3 + escalated share x 33.5 s
gemma4, SUT figures from the A2 memory check and the A1 baseline; the A2 speed tests replace them):

| Setting | Escalated | Wrong answers let through | Est. accuracy | Est. mean latency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gemma4 alone | 87/87 | - | 78.7/87 (90.4%) | 33.5 s |
| S1 | 60/87 (69%) | 0 | 81.0/87 (93.1%) | 25.2 s |
| S2 | 40/87 (46%) | 3 (Mortgage predicted for 2 Consumer loan, 1 Credit reporting) | 79.0/87 (90.8%) | 17.5 s |
| Not chosen: also accept Credit reporting | 21/87 (24%) | 8 | 76.0/87 (87.4%) | 10.2 s |

The third option was rejected because it falls below the per-category floor for Debt collection on the tuning set
(4 Debt collection tickets are predicted as Credit reporting and would be accepted).

## Known weaknesses

- **Small tuning counts.** The accept lists rest on 2 Money transfer and 5 Credit card predictions. The tuning set
  holds only 7 Money transfer and 8 Credit card tickets, while the test set holds 17 and 16, so more of phi3's
  Bank account confusions will appear on the test set than the tuning set showed.
- **The tuning set is easier than the test set** (gemma4 90.4% on tuning vs 78.4% on test in A1), so test-set
  accuracy is expected to be lower for every configuration.
- The answers above come from the A1 accuracy runs on P3's machine. phi3 gave identical answers in all three runs,
  and every tuning ticket that A1 load runs also sent to the official SUT got the same answer there: phi3 9/9
  tickets (47 answers over 9 runs), gemma4 2/2 (`analysis/output/a2_tuning.md`, last section).

## In the service

`server/classifier.py`, selected by environment: `OLLAMA_MODEL=phi3:3.8b`, `CASCADE_SETTING=s1` or `s2`,
`CASCADE_LARGE_MODEL=gemma4:e4b` (`CASCADE_SETTING=off` = a single model, as in A1). `GET /health` reports
`cascade` and `large_model`.

## What the service log records per ticket

Each `POST /tickets` line in `server/logs/access.log` carries, besides the A1 fields: `cascade` (s1/s2),
`small_answer` (phi3's category, `-` if none), `small_ms` (phi3 call, ms), `escalated` (0/1), `final_model` (the
model whose answer was returned) and `large_ms` (gemma4 call, only when escalated). The Ollama timing fields
(`ollama_total_ms`, `eval_tokens`, ...) describe the final model's call. The escalation fraction of a run =
lines with `escalated=1` / answered `POST /tickets` lines, counted from the service log.
